# trello-mcp

> A local Trello MCP server in Go. Stdio transport, compact curated responses, workspace allowlists and a read-only opt-in. Not the official Atlassian connector.

This file is an entrypoint index. The linked documents are the references.

- [Setup, one fetch for agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avhn/trello-mcp/main/docs/setup.md): install, register with seven clients, verify, update, roll back, uninstall.
- [Tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avhn/trello-mcp/main/docs/tools.md): tool behavior, parameters and synthetic examples; [compatibility policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avhn/trello-mcp/main/docs/tools.md#compatibility-and-versioning).
- [Configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avhn/trello-mcp/main/docs/configuration.md): variables, credential precedence, permissions, troubleshooting, security model.

Humans run the installer's quoted absolute-path auth command themselves in a private terminal, then reconnect or restart clients; Claude Desktop extension users enter the key and token in extension settings instead. Agents must never capture authentication output or request keys, tokens or authorization links.

Claude Desktop bundles support macOS and Windows amd64 (Windows on Arm is not claimed) and ship on normal releases; Linux Desktop remains beta. Download bundles from GitHub releases, verify checksums, and install/update manually. Registry discovery is separate from Desktop installation. Linux MCPBs are owner-untested beta downloads, excluded from Registry installation metadata; Linux users can use the CLI installer. Basic, detailed, metadata and performance health are local and access-unverified (policy health may make one best-effort workspace lookup), and metadata or policy details need configured credentials (unconfigured health returns only the setup response); use workspace_find {} for an actual Trello read. Desktop users need no CLI auth/status. Windows refuses local path uploads and attachment downloads even with directories configured.
